metadata.source: Research compilation — Wikidata Q-IDs verified via wikidata.org API
metadata.description: Japanese history expansion — Genpei War, Kamakura, Meiji Restoration, and WWII figures plus major media works. Expands beyond existing Sengoku coverage.

figures.name: Minamoto no Yoshitsune
figures.title: Samurai commander
figures.description: Legendary samurai whose brilliant military campaigns won the Genpei War for the Minamoto clan, only to be betrayed by his brother Yoritomo and die a tragic hero

figures.name: Minamoto no Yoritomo
figures.title: First Shogun of the Kamakura Shogunate
figures.description: Founded Japan's first military government, the Kamakura shogunate, establishing the samurai class as rulers of Japan for the next seven centuries

figures.name: Taira no Kiyomori
figures.title: Chancellor of the Realm
figures.description: First warrior to attain the position of Daijō-daijin (Chancellor), dominated the Imperial court until the Minamoto rebellion ended Taira supremacy

figures.name: Tomoe Gozen
figures.title: Female samurai warrior
figures.description: One of the few female warriors (onna-bugeisha) recorded in Japanese history, renowned for her bravery in the Genpei War fighting alongside Minamoto no Yoshinaka

figures.name: Miyamoto Musashi
figures.title: Swordsman and philosopher
figures.description: Japan's most famous swordsman, undefeated in over 60 duels, author of The Book of Five Rings, and a master calligrapher and painter in his later years

figures.name: Kusunoki Masashige
figures.title: Samurai and loyalist
figures.description: Paragon of samurai loyalty who fought to restore Emperor Go-Daigo to power, his final stand at Minatogawa became the ideal of bushido devotion

figures.name: Sei Shonagon
figures.title: Author and court lady
figures.description: Author of The Pillow Book, a witty and intimate journal of court life that stands alongside The Tale of Genji as a masterpiece of Heian literature

figures.name: Emperor Meiji
figures.title: Emperor of Japan
figures.description: Emperor whose reign transformed Japan from a feudal society into a modern industrial and military power through the Meiji Restoration

figures.name: Saigo Takamori
figures.title: Samurai and revolutionary
figures.description: One of the most influential samurai in Japanese history, helped overthrow the Tokugawa shogunate then led the failed Satsuma Rebellion, the last stand of the samurai class

figures.name: Tokugawa Yoshinobu
figures.title: 15th and last Shogun
figures.description: The last shogun of the Tokugawa dynasty, who resigned his position in 1867 and lived quietly through the Meiji era as Japan transformed around him

figures.name: Matthew C. Perry
figures.title: Commodore, United States Navy
figures.description: American naval officer whose Black Ships arrived in Edo Bay in 1853, forcing Japan to end over two centuries of isolation and open its ports to Western trade

figures.name: Sakamoto Ryoma
figures.title: Samurai and political activist
figures.description: Visionary samurai who brokered the alliance between rival domains that overthrew the Tokugawa shogunate, assassinated just before seeing the new Japan he helped create

figures.name: Ito Hirobumi
figures.title: First Prime Minister of Japan
figures.description: Principal architect of Japan's Meiji Constitution and four-time Prime Minister who shaped modern Japan's political institutions, assassinated in Harbin

figures.name: Emperor Hirohito
figures.title: Emperor of Japan
figures.description: The longest-reigning emperor of Japan, whose role during World War II remains debated — from figurehead to wartime leader, delivered the radio broadcast announcing Japan's surrender

figures.name: Hideki Tojo
figures.title: Prime Minister of Japan
figures.description: Prime Minister who led Japan into war against the United States, convicted as a Class A war criminal by the International Military Tribunal and executed

works.title: Seven Samurai
works.creator: Akira Kurosawa
works.description: Masterpiece about seven ronin hired to defend a farming village from bandits, widely regarded as one of the greatest and most influential films ever made

works.title: Ran
works.creator: Akira Kurosawa
works.description: Epic retelling of King Lear set in feudal Japan, following an aging warlord who divides his domain among his three sons with devastating consequences

works.title: Rashomon
works.creator: Akira Kurosawa
works.description: Revolutionary film presenting four contradictory accounts of a samurai's murder, introducing the 'Rashomon effect' concept to cinema and philosophy

works.title: Kagemusha
works.creator: Akira Kurosawa
works.description: A petty thief is recruited to impersonate the dying warlord Takeda Shingen, exploring themes of identity and the nature of power in Sengoku Japan

works.title: Yojimbo
works.creator: Akira Kurosawa
works.description: A wandering ronin arrives in a town divided by two rival crime bosses and plays them against each other, inspiring A Fistful of Dollars and countless imitators

works.title: Throne of Blood
works.creator: Akira Kurosawa
works.description: Shakespeare's Macbeth transposed to feudal Japan, with Toshiro Mifune as a samurai warrior driven to treachery by his wife's ambition and a spirit's prophecy

works.title: The Last Samurai
works.creator: Edward Zwick
works.description: An American military officer captured during the Satsuma Rebellion comes to respect the samurai way of life, loosely inspired by the true story of Jules Brunet

works.title: Memoirs of a Geisha
works.creator: Rob Marshall
works.description: A young girl sold into a geisha house rises to become one of Japan's most celebrated geisha, set against the backdrop of pre-war and wartime Japan

works.title: Silence
works.creator: Martin Scorsese
works.description: Two Jesuit priests travel to 17th-century Japan seeking their missing mentor, facing persecution and a crisis of faith during the brutal suppression of Christianity

works.title: Ghost of Tsushima
works.creator: Sucker Punch Productions
works.description: Open-world action game set during the first Mongol invasion of Japan, following a samurai who must abandon tradition to become a guerrilla warrior

works.title: Shogun (novel)
works.creator: James Clavell
works.description: Epic historical novel about an English navigator shipwrecked in Japan during the power struggle that led to the Tokugawa shogunate, based on the life of William Adams

works.title: Shogun (TV series)
works.creator: Rachel Kondo
works.description: Critically acclaimed adaptation of James Clavell's novel depicting the political intrigue and cultural clash in feudal Japan through the eyes of an English sailor

properties.notes: Yoshitsune's story inspired Ran's themes of fraternal betrayal
Takeda Shingen is the warlord being impersonated in Kagemusha
Katsumoto character inspired by Saigo Takamori
Nobunaga appears as the rival warlord
Blackthorne character based on William Adams
Toranaga character based on Tokugawa Ieyasu
